description.shortText: A solar cell that combines two types of perovskite merged into a single photovoltaic cell. It is a low-cost alternative to conventional solar cell technologies, able to capture sunlight and efficiently convert it into electricity.

attachments.name: Major advance in solar cells made from cheap, easy-to-use perovskite
attachments.description: Solar cells made from an inexpensive and increasingly popular material called perovskite can more efficiently turn sunlight into electricity using a new technique to sandwich two types of perovskite into a single photovoltaic cell.

attachments.name: A molecularly engineered hole-transporting material for efficient perovskite solar cells
attachments.description: Solution-processable perovskite solar cells have recently achieved certified power conversion efficiencies of over 20%, challenging the long-standing perception that high efficiencies must come at high costs. One major bottleneck for increasing the efficiency even further is the lack of suitable hole-transporting materials, which extract positive charges from the active light absorber and transmit them to the electrode. In this work, we present a molecularly engineered hole-transport material with a simple dissymmetric fluorene–dithiophene (FDT) core substituted by N,N-di-p-methoxyphenylamine donor groups, which can be easily modified, providing the blueprint for a family of potentially low-cost hole-transport materials. We use FDT on state-of-the-art devices and achieve power conversion efficiencies of 20.2% which compare favourably with control devices with 2,2′,7,7′-tetrakis(N,N-di-p-methoxyphenylamine)-9,9′-spirobifluorene (spiro-OMeTAD). Thus, this new hole transporter has the potential to replace spiro-OMeTAD.

attachments.name: High Efficiency, Low-Cost Perovskite Solar Cell Modules
attachments.description: Discovery of solution-processed mm- scale single-crystal growth of hybrid perovskites

attachments.name: Perovskite-perovskite tandem photovoltaics with optimized band gaps
attachments.description: The ready processability of organic-inorganic perovskite materials for solar cells should enable the fabrication of tandem solar cells, in which the top layer is tuned to absorb shorter wavelengths and the lower layer to absorb the remaining longer-wavelength light. The difficulty in making an all-perovskite cell is finding a material that absorbs the red end of the spectrum. Eperon et al. developed an infrared-absorbing mixed tin-lead material that can deliver 14.8% efficiency on its own and 20.3% efficiency in a four-terminal tandem cell.
